earlier_findings.evidence: PREREG v3 section 1 'Per question': Q1 is a model test only if max(|dF_pred(4)|, |dF_pred(8)|) >= 0.02, else the fixed label (text in PREREG equals ghz3_run.Q1_LABEL). c1_check returns q1_max_abs_delta_F_pred_4_8 and q1_model_test; calibration_check.json records them and the label; the analysis attaches the label (run_analysis, q1 block) and reports the in-use value too. The C-1(b) justification no longer claims 0.02 exceeds the drift ('close to the run-1/run-2 drift at small n (0.022)'). Tests: TestRunnerFlows.test_q1_replicate_label_is_recorded..., TestAnalysisRehearsal.test_q1_replicate_label... and test_q1_snapshot_and_in_use_values_are_both_reported. Residual: which predictions decide the label in the 'calibration changed' case is not stated in the text (T4, minor).

All four fixes asked for are in place. (1) A passing --dry-run is binding (PREREG section 1); stopping_rule_report flags a passing dry-run (exit 0) without a passing submit within 2 h, so case A of the second look is now reported. (2) Attempts are defined (modes submit-refused/failed/accepted; quota-invalid and job.json-exists lines are submit-not-attempt) and any attempt after a refused one on the same UTC day is a deviation, as the v3 text says; cases C, D, E behave as the v3 text defines (TestLogReport). (3) Log lines hold predictions_sha256, never the predictions (test_log_lines_carry_a_hash...); the log now also holds max_abs_delta_F_pred and q1_model_test (magnitudes only). (4) job.json records dryrun_log_lines and dryrun_log_sha256; log_prefix_status is a K3 item. Residual: the binding clause can still be side-stepped with a deliberately low --quota-seconds (C-1 PASS is printed, the run is not 'passing', no deviation) or a Ctrl-C between the PASS lines and the log line; this reveals no prediction (T1, minor). Post-anchor lines are not validated (T2, minor).

assemble_answer builds the answer from Q1_SENTENCES (H1 outcome and reading), Q2_SENTENCES (H4 outcome and reading) and JOINT_SENTENCES (only the four definite combinations), then the labels; both readings are passed (run_analysis 'reads'). All sentences equal the PREREG section 4 tables verbatim (checked programmatically). TestVerdictMapping.test_all_sixteen_combinations checks every outcome/reading pair of H1 and H4, test_readings_of_both_criteria_are_passed covers the old H4 'not demonstrated' defect, and control failure gives 'yorumlanamaz' for all 16.

snapshot_at saves calibration_dates(properties(datetime=start)) with the history result; history_dates_ok rejects a history result unless every M2-input date of S_48 is at or before the execution start (then the fallback applies); changed_inputs_have_later_dates requires every differing input (gate error per edge/gate, T1/T2/readout per qubit, any gate_length for an idle time) to carry a later date than the dates recorded at submission (select_m2_dates in calibration_check.json), else 'execution-time calibration not verified' with the snapshot's predictions. save_execution_calibration writes a new execution_calibration_<utc>[_k].json on every fetch; the analysis uses the first. Test with a service that ignores the datetime: TestFetchExecutionCalibration.test_a_service_that_ignores_the_datetime_cannot_make_a_later_calibration_primary. In qiskit-ibm-runtime 0.52.0, target_history(datetime) is convert_to_target(configuration, properties(datetime=datetime)), so values and dates come from the same kind of query. Residuals: fetch attempts are not logged, so deleting the first file is undetectable (T2); an execution start before the submission time is not detected (T3); a history result that passes the date check but cannot be used does not fall through to the saved current calibration (T6). All minor.

power_file_status compares the recorded input hashes with the frozen certs/power.json (run-1 and run-2 data files) and FREEZE_GHZ3.json (study files) and with the files now, checks the predictions are the snapshot's, and recomputes the power from the snapshot's predictions (2000 datasets, seed 20261116) requiring equality of the whole record (_close, tol 1e-9); each is a K3 item. PREREG section 4: 'The readings use the power at submission, computed on the snapshot's predictions, in every case of section 3'; run_analysis uses pw_status['power'] in every case. Tests: TestAnalysisRehearsal.test_power_file_k3_items, test_power_recomputation_default_is_the_registered_2000_datasets. Residual: the equality is bit-level and no software versions are recorded (T7, minor).

The printing tests now run the real build_and_report (only core internals patched): my mutation (show_model=True in both cmd_dry_run and cmd_submit) makes test_nothing_of_the_model_is_printed_by_the_real_build_and_report, test_submit_passes_records_everything_and_prints_no_prediction_or_power and test_dry_run_prints_only_pass_fail_and_logs fail. The job.json-exists refusal logs the parsed quota (quota_p), asserted in the submit test.

cmd_submit wraps the temporary-folder and submission block in except BaseException: the folder is kept as attempt_<utc> (_keep_attempt), a submit-failed line with the job id (if one was returned) is logged, KeyboardInterrupt is re-raised, else exit 8. PREREG section 1 and README step 5b require checking the account's job list before any retry; --recover JOBID moves the kept files into run/ and writes job.json (recovered: true) without submitting. Tests cover failure, interrupt, retry, recover, recover after a failed move, refusals. Residuals: an interrupt in the few seconds between the PASS lines and that block (power computation) is not logged (T1); --recover does not check that the job belongs to the attempt (T3). Both minor.

PREREG section 4 now lists 'independent symmetric readout error beyond the model (it lowers C about twice as much as P)' among the opposite-direction classes; the factor is right (C scales with prod(1 - 2 eps), P with prod(1 - eps)).

(a) Joint (FAILS, FAILS) sentence is now 'M2 misses the small-n band and does not overpredict at every n'. (b) K2 is binding in the analysis on run/circuits.qpy (k2_noiseless), the FakeKingston check is a design check. (c) ghz3_d4.py docstring: 'simulator and run-1 and run-2 data only'. (d) The tracking rows carry ci_kind 'shot noise only' and sigma_d_F. (e) The REVISIONS N9 row records that the F3 row's 'no fails reading' is superseded by clarification 3. Other stale 'v2' strings remain (T5, minor).

The part left open in the second look (Q1 could again be a data replicate) is closed by the per-question rule of N1: C-1 uses the n = 48 M2 inputs and max_n |dF_pred| >= 0.02 for the run, and Q1 carries a fixed replicate label unless max(|dF_pred(4)|, |dF_pred(8)|) >= 0.02. On FakeKingston the n = 48 gate inputs contain those of every smaller n and S_n is in S_48, so 'the n = 48 components contain every smaller n' holds for the gate and qubit inputs.

Closed by N3: every combination of H1 and H4 outcome and reading maps to pre-written sentences, the control row gives 'yorumlanamaz', UNDEFINED rows give 'not answered', and both readings are used; all 16 combinations are tested.

Closed by N4: the history path is date-verified against the execution start and against the submission dates, --fetch never overwrites (every attempt kept, the first used), and PREREG section 4 states that the readings use the submission power on the snapshot's predictions in every section 3 case. The fallback is date-checked from the refreshed current properties, so a cached Target cannot give a false 'verified'. Minor residuals in T2, T3, T6.

Closed by N2: predictions are neither printed nor logged (hash only), every dry-run and submit that reaches the checks is logged, the log is anchored in job.json and checked as K3, a passing dry-run is binding, and the report implements the deviations as written. The timing freedom left (T1) reveals pass/fail of C-1 only, not a prediction.

new_findings.location: ghz3_run.py _refusal (791-799), cmd_dry_run (802-821), cmd_submit (863-898: the power computation at 879-887 catches Exception only and runs before the BaseException block that starts at 900), main (1185-1195); ghz3_analyze.py stopping_rule_report (345-350); PREREG section 1, stopping rule
new_findings.finding: The binding clause and the 'first passing --submit is the run' rule can be side-stepped without a reported deviation. (a) 'Passing' is exit code 0, and a dry run with --quota-seconds below 1.15 x estimate ends with exit 6 although it prints 'C-1 (new calibration for M2): PASS' (and logs q1_model_test and max |dF_pred|); it is not binding and never a deviation. The same works once per UTC day with --submit --quota-seconds 1 (a refused attempt, allowed). (b) A Ctrl-C after the PASS lines and before the BaseException block (about 3 s of power computation plus the date lookup; about 1 s of usage query in --dry-run) leaves no log line and no folder, so an attempt that passed every check vanishes. (c) The text says every --dry-run and every --submit appends a line, but freeze or code-identity refusals, an invalid --dry-run quota, and failures before the checks (backend selection, build) write none. (d) The 2-hour window is measured between log-write times; the accepted line is written after the power computation and the upload, so a submit started just under 2 h after the dry run can be flagged.
new_findings.evidence: scratch\check_v3_paths.py: L1 two dry runs with quota 1 -> exit [6, 6], C-1 PASS printed, deviations []; L2 three daily --submit --quota-seconds 1 -> (6, PASS) each, then an accepted submit on day 4, deviations []; L3 KeyboardInterrupt raised from compute_power after the PASS lines -> 0 log lines, no attempt folder, deviations []. compute_power with 2000 datasets takes 3.2 s on this machine. No prediction is revealed by any of these routes, which is why this is minor.
new_findings.suggested_fix: Define 'passing' for the binding clause as 'D-7 and C-1 pass' whatever C-2 says (or drop C-2 from --dry-run), and have stopping_rule_report use the logged d7/c1 results instead of exit_code == 0; report every line whose C-1 passed but whose C-2 failed, with the quota given. In cmd_submit, append a 'checks-passed' line right after _checks (or extend the BaseException handler to cover everything after the checks) so an interrupted passing attempt is recorded. Either log the pre-check refusals as not-attempts or change the text to 'every --dry-run and --submit that reaches the checks'. Measure the 2 h window from the attempt's start time (log the snapshot utc in each line).

new_findings.location: ghz3_analyze.py log_prefix_status (359-376), stopping_rule_report (325-356), execution_calibration (574-582); ghz3_run.py cmd_submit (917, 941), save_execution_calibration / cmd_fetch (1076-1167)
new_findings.finding: Two integrity gaps in the records added for v3. (a) The log anchor protects only the lines before the accepted submit; lines after it (including the accepted line) are used by the deviation report without any check, and their 'utc' is self-reported, so a back-dated line appended later can erase a deviation while the anchor check still passes. (b) Fetch attempts leave no trace outside their own files: nothing records how many execution_calibration_*.json files were written or their hashes, so the 'first attempt is used' rule cannot be checked; deleting the first file would go unnoticed. In the rare case of a recalibration between submission and execution, an early and a late fetch can give 'calibration changed before execution' (execution-time predictions primary) and 'not verified' (snapshot predictions primary), i.e. a choice between two prediction sets after the data. The anchor itself sits in job.json, which the same author writes; it detects accidental, not deliberate, edits.
new_findings.evidence: scratch\check_v3_paths.py P: passing dry run 08:00, accepted submit 11:00 -> deviation reported; after appending {'utc': '20261120T090000Z', 'mode': 'submit-failed', ...} the deviation list is [] and log_prefix_status is ok with 2 lines after the anchor. cmd_fetch appends no line to run/dryrun_log.jsonl; execution_calibration takes files[0] of whatever is in run/.
new_findings.suggested_fix: In the analysis, treat a post-anchor line whose utc is earlier than the anchor time (job.json submitted_utc) as a K3 failure, and count only anchored lines plus the accepted line. Let --fetch append a 'fetch' line to the log with the attempt file name and its SHA-256, and have the analysis use the first logged attempt and require its file and hash. Optionally publish job.json and the log right after submission, which is the only anchor the author cannot rewrite.

new_findings.location: ghz3_run.py cmd_recover (947-1011, the service read at 983-990 is information only); ghz3_analyze.py run_analysis K3 block (759-795) and execution_calibration (593-606)
new_findings.finding: --recover JOBID accepts any job id. It reads the job's status and backend but does not compare the backend with the attempt's, nor the job's creation time with the attempt time, nor its number of pubs; and the analysis has no K3 item that the job was created and ran after submitted_utc. Run 2's job has 368 pubs with the same circuit names, so a mistyped or misread id (for example run 2's job, the previous one in the account's list) would pass --fetch and K3 and be analysed as run 3, with only the 'execution-time calibration not verified' label.
new_findings.evidence: scratch\check_v3_paths.py R: after an exit-8 attempt on fake_kingston, cmd_recover with a job whose backend is 'ibm_other_device' returns 0 and writes job.json (backend fake_kingston, recovered_service_read backend ibm_other_device). E2: an execution-calibration record with the execution start one day before submitted_utc and values equal to the snapshot gives status 'equal', label None.
new_findings.suggested_fix: In --recover, refuse unless the service read succeeds and the job's backend equals the attempt's, the job was created at or after the attempt's submitted_utc (and before the exit-8 log line plus a margin), and it has 368 pubs. In the analysis, add a K3 item: the job's 'created' and execution start timestamps are at or after job.json submitted_utc.

new_findings.location: PREREG section 1 'Per question' and section 4 Q1 table; ghz3_analyze.py run_analysis q1 block (848-862)

The code decides it on the snapshot's predictions, also when section 3 makes the execution-time predictions primary (H1 is then evaluated on predictions whose small-n change from run 2 may differ); the PREREG does not say which. new_findings.suggested_fix: Add one sentence to PREREG section 1 naming the predictions that decide the Q1 label (the snapshot's, as coded, or the predictions in use). Optionally give the replicate case its own Q1 wording (or drop 'on a new calibration' from the Q1 sentences) and reword the label on a device change ('small-n predictions within 0.02 of run 2's').

new_findings.location: ghz3_run.py line 1, 165, 484, 667, 680; ghz3_analyze.py lines 1-12; ghz3_d4.py 191, 206; tests_ghz3.py line 1 and 2499; PREREG section 1 'Atomic writes'

Module docstrings still cite 'PREREG.md v2'; compute_power writes 'prereg': 'run 3 section 4 (rule 16), PREREG v2' into power_run3.json and certs/power.json; the selftest prints 'C-1 (v2) logic' (and a test asserts that text); the ghz3_analyze docstring still names 'run/execution_calibration.json' and says K2 is read from certs/k2_sim.json, omitting the binding K2. new_findings.suggested_fix: Update the strings to v3 (changing the compute_power 'prereg' string changes certs/power.json: rerun ghz3_d4.py and the tests before the freeze), and say 'exit 8, or the interrupt is re-raised' in the PREREG.

new_findings.finding: A history result that passes the date check but cannot be used (M2 cannot be computed on it, or its snapshot hash does not match) ends as 'unavailable' through the outer except or an early return, without trying the saved current calibration. The outcome is conservative (snapshot predictions, 'not verified'), but a verifiable 'no recalibration since submission' is lost, and PREREG section 3 describes the fallback for a history result that cannot be accepted.
new_findings.evidence: scratch\check_v3_paths.py E1: history snapshot with t1 = None on one qubit of S_48 plus a verifiable current calibration -> ('unavailable', 'execution-time calibration not verified', 'execution-time calibration could not be used (TypeError)'); the same current calibration alone -> 'verified_no_recalibration'.
new_findings.suggested_fix: Treat any failure of the history path as 'history unavailable' (set note, fall through to the current-calibration block) instead of returning.

new_findings.finding: K3 now requires the analysis's recomputation of the power to equal power_run3.json within 1e-9 over the whole record, including the integer tallies of 12000 simulated datasets. That needs a bit-reproducible environment between submission and analysis (same numpy Generator stream, same libm), but the power file records no software versions. A changed numpy or platform could flip one simulated dataset and make the whole run 'yorumlanamaz', with no record to diagnose it.
new_findings.evidence: same = pw.get('n_datasets') == n_datasets and pw.get('seed') == POWER_SEED and _close(exp, pw); compute_power stores no numpy/qiskit/python versions. Within this environment the recomputation is exact (d4 reproduces certs/power.json byte for byte).
new_findings.suggested_fix: Record numpy, scipy, qiskit and python versions and the platform in power_run3.json (and job.json), and state in PREREG section 4 that the analysis runs in the same environment; a version mismatch is then a diagnosable K3 cause rather than a silent one.

new_findings.location: ghz3_run.py cmd_submit (no K2 before _submit_job); ghz3_analyze.py k2_noiseless (134-151); PREREG section 5 K2
new_findings.finding: The binding K2 runs only in the analysis, after the QPU time is spent. A transpilation defect on the new device or calibration would be found only then and would make the run 'yorumlanamaz'. The same noiseless check of the circuits about to be submitted could run before submission.
new_findings.evidence: k2_noiseless is called only from run_analysis; the check takes about 30 s and needs no account. On FakeKingston the margins are large (F_sim >= 0.999, C_mix,sim <= 0.006), so a failure is unlikely.
new_findings.suggested_fix: Optionally run k2_noiseless in --submit (and --dry-run) before submitting and refuse on failure as a refused attempt like D-7; keep the analysis's K2 as the binding record.

checks_without_findings: Code identity: ghz2_core.py and ghz2_study.py equal run 2's FREEZE_GHZ2.json values; the certificates' study hashes equal ghz3_study_h4.py and ghz2_study.py.
Answer and label strings in the code equal the PREREG v3 text verbatim (whitespace normalised).
Deviation report: the second look's cases A-F give the results the v3 text defines.

Execution-time calibration: the history acceptance and 'changed' logic match PREREG section 3; in qiskit-ibm-runtime 0.52.0, IBMBackend.target caches its Target and properties(refresh=True) does not rebuild it, but the fallback takes its dates from the refreshed properties and requires every M2-input date before the submission, so a cached Target cannot produce a false 'verified'.
m2_gate_keys walks the transpiled circuits in the same order and with the same skips as core._one_q_errors, so cz_err[i] and g1_*_err[i] are dated against the right gates.

Power-file checks: input hashes against certs/power.json and FREEZE_GHZ3.json, predictions against the snapshot, recomputation; all wired into K3, and readings use the submission power in every section 3 case.
No refusal path submits anything or writes outside run/ (plus the kept attempt folder after a submission failure).
